signaling-layer.description: WebSocket-based message passing between the browser client and the JVM server. All messages are typed `Packet` instances serialized to JSON.

required_patterns.packet-codec: All messages must be subclasses of `screenshare.common.Packet` and annotated with `@Serializable` + `@SerialName`. Encoding/decoding always uses `Json.encodeToString` / `Json.decodeFromString<Packet>`.
required_patterns.client-sends-packet: Client always calls `WebsocketService.sendPacket(packet)` which writes a `Text` WebSocket frame.
required_patterns.server-receives-packet: Server receives frames in `Application.module()`, deserializes to `Packet`, dispatches `JoinRoom` directly or delegates to `Room.consumePacket(user, packet)`.
required_patterns.server-sends-packet: Server sends to a single peer via `RoomUser.sendPacket(packet)` or to all via `Room.broadcast(packet)`.

architectural_constraints.common-module-only: New packet types must be defined in the `common` module only, so they are available on both client and server.
architectural_constraints.side-enforcement: `Packet.getSide()` returns `CLIENT` or `SERVER`. The server ignores server-side packets; the client only processes server-side packets.
architectural_constraints.no-http-rest: There are no REST endpoints; all client↔server communication is exclusively over the single WebSocket connection.

room-management.description: Server-side in-memory model of active rooms and their participants. `Room` holds a mutable map of `RoomUser` objects and a chat history list.

required_patterns.room-lifecycle: `Room` is created lazily on first `JoinRoom`, removed when the last user disconnects.
required_patterns.packet-dispatch: All client packets (except `JoinRoom`) are routed through `Room.consumePacket(user, packet)` with a `when` expression.
required_patterns.broadcast: Notifications to all users use `Room.broadcast(packet)`, which iterates `users.values` and calls `RoomUser.sendPacket`.
required_patterns.targeted-send: WebRTC signaling packets (`SendIceCandidate`, `SendDescription`) are forwarded to a single target user by socket ID.

architectural_constraints.in-memory-only: No database or persistence layer; room state is lost on server restart.
architectural_constraints.mutable-maps: Users are stored in `MutableMap<String, RoomUser>` keyed by socket ID.

webrtc-peer-connections.description: Client-side management of `RTCPeerConnection` objects, one per remote peer. All WebRTC API interaction is wrapped inside `RTCPeerConnectionDecorator`.

required_patterns.decorator-pattern: All interactions with the browser's `RTCPeerConnection` object must go through `RTCPeerConnectionDecorator`. Raw `dynamic` access to WebRTC APIs is prohibited outside the `decorators/` package.
required_patterns.offer-answer-flow: The peer that connects first (or calls `recreatePeerConnections`) is the initiator; it creates an offer via `peerConnection.createOffer()`, sets its local description, and sends it via `WebsocketService.sendDescription()`.
required_patterns.ice-relay: ICE candidates are exchanged through the server: `onIceCandidateAdd` → `WebsocketService.sendIceCandidate()` → server → `IceCandidateReceived` → `PeerConnections.updateIceCandidate()`.
required_patterns.track-management: `PeerConnections.addTracksIfNotPresent()` adds screen and mic tracks to all peer connections before creating offers; it checks for duplicates using `RTCPeerConnectionDecorator.hasTrack()`.

architectural_constraints.google-stun: ICE servers are hardcoded to `stun:stun1.l.google.com:19302` and `stun:stun2.l.google.com:19302` inside `RTCPeerConnectionDecorator.instantiate()`.
architectural_constraints.no-media-server: There is no SFU/MCU; all media is point-to-point (full mesh topology between peers in the room).
architectural_constraints.screen-vs-audio: Stream type is inferred from track type: a stream with video tracks is treated as screen-share; audio-only streams are treated as mic audio.

ui.description: Browser DOM manipulation written in Kotlin/JS. Split into three layers: element references (`Elements`), mutations (`InterfaceMutations`, `UserListMutations`), and event handler registration (`InterfaceHandlers`).

required_patterns.elements-singleton: All DOM element references are centralized in the `Elements` singleton object, retrieved once at startup via `document.getElementById` wrapped in the typed `getElement<T>()` helper.
required_patterns.mutation-objects: DOM modifications are grouped in `object InterfaceMutations` and `object UserListMutations`. Direct DOM manipulation anywhere else in the codebase is avoided.
required_patterns.handler-registration: All UI event listener registrations live in `InterfaceHandlers.kt` and are triggered by calling `registerUIHandlers(...)` from `main()`.
required_patterns.daisyui-classes: UI styling uses DaisyUI utility classes (e.g., `btn`, `chat`, `chat-bubble`, `badge`, `hidden`, `animate-fade-in`). CSS class toggling is the mechanism for show/hide and state changes.

architectural_constraints.no-virtual-dom: There is no React, Vue, or other virtual DOM framework. All DOM operations are direct (`document.createElement`, `classList.add/remove`, `innerHTML`, `appendChild`).
architectural_constraints.tailwind-daisyui-cdn: TailwindCSS and DaisyUI are loaded from CDN in `index.html`; there is no local CSS build pipeline.
architectural_constraints.language: UI text is in Brazilian Portuguese (pt-BR); new UI strings should match this convention.

client-session.description: The `Session` class aggregates all client-side state and coordinates service objects (`VoiceChat`, `ScreenSharing`, `PeerConnections`, `WebsocketService`). It is a `CoroutineScope` delegate.

required_patterns.single-session: There is at most one `Session` instance, held in the global `session` variable in `Main.kt`. It is created when the user clicks 'Join Room'.
required_patterns.coroutine-scope-delegation: `Session` delegates `CoroutineScope` to the passed-in `coroutineScope`, so all `launch {}` calls inside `Session` use the same dispatcher.
required_patterns.action-methods: User-triggered actions (send message, toggle mic, start/stop screen share) are `fun handleX(): Job` that `launch {}` coroutines.

architectural_constraints.global-var: The global `session` variable can be null before the user joins a room. Code that needs it calls `getSessionOrAlert()` which throws `IllegalStateException` with an alert if null.
architectural_constraints.no-di-framework: There is no dependency injection framework; service objects are created explicitly inside `Session`'s constructor body.

media-capture.description: Browser `MediaStream` capture for both screen (via `getDisplayMedia`) and microphone (via `getUserMedia`). Audio level monitoring uses the Web Audio API.

required_patterns.display-media-decorator: `window.navigator.mediaDevices.getDisplayMedia()` must be called through the extension function in `DisplayMediaDecorator.kt` because the standard Kotlin browser bindings do not expose this method.
required_patterns.audio-monitoring: Audio level monitoring (speaking indicator) is implemented using `AudioContext`, `createMediaStreamSource`, and `createAnalyser` via raw `js(...)` interop inside `VoiceChat.kt`.
required_patterns.track-lifecycle: When a local screen track ends (user stops sharing via browser UI), the `onended` callback triggers `onStreamEnd()` to clean up and signal the server.

architectural_constraints.no-constraints-abstraction: Media constraints are constructed inline inside `buildMediaStreamConstraints()` methods in `ScreenSharing` and `VoiceChat`; they use `mapOf<String, Any>` passed as JS-compatible objects.
architectural_constraints.dynamic-audio-api: Web Audio API is not typed in Kotlin Wrappers; it is accessed via `js("new AudioContext()").unsafeCast<dynamic>()`.

multiplatform-common.description: The `common` Gradle module targets both JS and JVM. It contains only shared data models and the packet protocol.

required_patterns.kmp-only-apis: Code in `common` must only use Kotlin standard library and `kotlinx.serialization`. No platform-specific APIs allowed.
required_patterns.serialization-annotations: All shared data classes use `@Serializable`. Packet subclasses additionally use `@SerialName` with explicit compact JSON keys (e.g., `"rid"`, `"sid"`, `"msg"`) to minimize payload size.

architectural_constraints.no-ui-no-server-logic: The `common` module must not contain UI code or server-specific logic.
architectural_constraints.ksp-present: KSP is applied to the `common` module in `build.gradle.kts` but currently used only for potential annotation processing, not for any active code generation visible in source.

deployment.description: The application is packaged as a fat JAR (via the `ktor` plugin) in `server-java`, containerized with Docker, and deployed to Fly.io.

required_patterns.client-bundled-into-server: Before the server JAR is built, the `copyClientToServer` Gradle task copies the Webpack-bundled `clientApp.js` and `index.html` into `server/src/jvmMain/resources/static/`, which Ktor serves as static resources.
required_patterns.static-resources: Ktor serves the frontend via `staticResources()` routing; the client app is a single-page application loaded from the root path.

architectural_constraints.single-port: Both the WebSocket signaling endpoint (`/`) and the static frontend are served on the same HTTP port (8080).
architectural_constraints.fly-region: Fly.io deployment is configured for the `gru` (São Paulo) region.
